title: Number Theory & Combinatorics Quick Revision
summary: Quick revision notes on modular arithmetic and overflow, GCD/LCM, primes and the sieve, fast exponentiation, modular inverse and nCr, built for competitive programming and interviews.

chapters.title: Modulo and Overflow: The Mental Model
points: Definition: a mod m is the remainder in [0, m-1]; a ≡ b (mod m) means m divides (a-b)
Add, subtract and multiply can be reduced mod m at every step: (a*b) % m = ((a%m)*(b%m)) % m
Division is NOT allowed directly: (a/b) % m ≠ (a%m)/(b%m); use the modular inverse instead
Negative operands: in C++/Java, -7 % 5 = -2; fix with ((a % m) + m) % m to get 3
Standard modulus 1e9+7 is prime; a*b with both below 1e9+7 reaches about 1e18, so use 64-bit (long long) and reduce after each multiply

chapters.title: GCD, Euclid and LCM
points: Euclid: gcd(a,b) = gcd(b, a % b), stop when b = 0 and return a; gcd(0,x)=x
Code: int gcd(int a,int b){ return b==0 ? a : gcd(b, a%b); } or std::gcd in C++17
Time is O(log(min(a,b))) because the remainder at least halves every two steps
LCM: lcm(a,b) = a / gcd(a,b) * b; divide first to avoid overflow, never a*b/gcd
Extended Euclid finds x,y with ax + by = gcd(a,b); it is the base of the modular inverse; gcd(a,b)*lcm(a,b) = a*b

chapters.title: Primes and the Sieve of Eratosthenes
points: Prime test by trial division: check divisors i with i*i <= n, O(sqrt n); handle n < 2 as not prime
Sieve: mark every multiple of each prime p as composite, starting at p*p, for p up to sqrt(n)
Sieve complexity is O(n log log n) time and O(n) memory; use it for all primes up to about 1e7
Code: vector<bool> comp(n+1); for(i=2;i*i<=n;i++) if(!comp[i]) for(j=i*i;j<=n;j+=i) comp[j]=true;
Smallest-prime-factor sieve stores spf[x], giving prime factorization of any x <= n in O(log x)
Mistake: starting the inner loop at 2*i wastes time, and i*i overflows int when n is near 2^31; use long long

chapters.title: Fast Exponentiation (Binary Power)
points: Idea: a^n = (a^(n/2))^2 for even n, and a * a^(n-1) for odd n, so O(log n) multiplies instead of O(n)
Iterative: res=1; while(n){ if(n&1) res=res*a%m; a=a*a%m; n>>=1; }
Reduce a with a %= m before the loop and keep res and a as long long
Example: 3^13 mod m uses bits 1101, so it multiplies in 3^1, 3^4 and 3^8
Works for matrix power too (Fibonacci in O(log n)); a modulus near 1e18 needs __int128 or mulmod to avoid overflow

chapters.title: Modular Inverse and nCr
points: Inverse of a mod m is x with a*x ≡ 1 (mod m); it exists only if gcd(a,m) = 1
Prime m (Fermat): inverse = a^(m-2) mod m, computed with fast exponentiation in O(log m)
Composite m: use extended Euclid to get the inverse; Fermat does not apply
nCr = n! / (r!(n-r)!); precompute fact[] and invFact[] up to N, then answer each query in O(1) as fact[n]*invFact[r]%m*invFact[n-r]%m
Build invFact[N] = pow(fact[N], m-2), then invFact[i-1] = invFact[i]*i % m, so only one exponentiation is needed
Pascal: C(n,r) = C(n-1,r-1) + C(n-1,r) in O(n*r), works for any modulus; mistakes: n! mod m is 0 once n >= m, and r > n must return 0

chapters.title: Cheat Sheet: Number Theory Toolkit
points: Mod rules: reduce after each + - *; fix negatives with ((a%m)+m)%m; never divide, use the inverse
Overflow rule: products need long long; lcm = a/gcd*b; use __int128 for modulus above 3e9
gcd(a,b) = gcd(b,a%b), O(log n); gcd*lcm = a*b
Sieve O(n log log n), start at i*i; trial division O(sqrt n); spf sieve for factorization
powmod O(log n); inverse = a^(m-2) for prime m; nCr = fact*invFact*invFact in O(1) after O(N) setup
